cards.front: Recall a key point about Composition Techniques and Development
cards.back: Successful compositions show DEVELOPMENT, not just repetition — musical ideas are extended, varied, transformed and combined across sections.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Composition Techniques and Development
cards.back: Structural planning before composing: decide on form, key relationships, textural changes and dynamic shape — this prevents aimless meandering.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Composition Techniques and Development
cards.back: Contrasting sections create musical interest: vary texture (thick/thin), dynamics (loud/soft), harmony (tense/resolved), melody (legato/staccato).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Composition Techniques and Development
cards.back: Linking to Areas of Study strengthens your composition: use elements from your chosen AoS as inspiration for style, harmony and structure.

cards.front: What should you know about music exam tips?
cards.back: Plan structure BEFORE composing. Show DEVELOPMENT of ideas (not just repetition). Reference AoS influences. Vary texture and dynamics. Write idiomatically for instruments.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: A composition just means writing some music that sounds good. Correct: AO2 assesses TECHNICAL CONTROL and COHERENCE — the composition must demonstrate deliberate musical choices, logical development of ideas, structural coherence, and effective use of musical elements. Writing whatever sounds good without understanding why will score poorly.
Plan a composition in a style influenced by one of your Areas of Study. Outline the structure, key features and how you will develop your musical ideas across the piece.

cards.front: Assessment Objective Focus: Composition Techniques and Development
cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Show knowledge of Composition Techniques and Development using appropriate musical vocabulary (e.g. terminology for elements, devices, and contexts).

cards.back: In the AQA GCSE Music listening exam, questions about composition techniques and development typically ask you to: identify features by ear; describe how they are used; explain their effect; compare features between extracts.
